excerpt: Nansen is a Singapore-based onchain analytics platform that labels hundreds of millions of crypto wallets so traders can follow 'smart money', and now lets users trade from the same app. Backed by a16z and Accel.
content:
Nansen analyses public blockchain data and attaches labels to wallet addresses, such as exchanges, funds, known traders and protocols, so investors can see who is moving money and where. Its best-known idea is "smart money": tracking wallets with a strong record so users can see what experienced crypto investors are buying or selling. Its website now describes the product as a way to trade everything onchain with AI, powered by more than 500 million labelled addresses, with tools to track smart money, analyse any token and execute trades in one place, plus a mobile app and the Nansen Wallet.

Nansen is based in Singapore and led by CEO Alex Svanevik. In June 2021 TechCrunch reported that it raised a $12 million Series A led by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), and that its dashboards then analysed some 90 million Ethereum wallets for crypto traders and hedge funds. DealStreetAsia reported that Skyfall Ventures, Coinbase Ventures, imToken Ventures, Mechanism Capital and QCP Capital also joined, and that Svanevik planned to double headcount from 30 to 60 by the end of the year. In December 2021 The Block reported that Nansen had raised fresh funding led by Accel at a $750 million valuation, citing investors close to the deal; Nansen did not comment on the valuation at the time.

Nansen sells subscriptions, and its plans are shown inside the app rather than on a public pricing page; when we checked, its plans link redirected to an account page that requires sign-in, so we do not quote prices. Crypto assets are volatile and trading them carries a high risk of loss. Nothing on this page is investment advice.

This profile draws on Nansen's own site and published reporting. We have not tested the product, and nothing here is paid placement.

use_cases: Following what labelled smart-money wallets are buying and selling
Researching a token's holders and flows before investing
Screening tokens across chains by activity
Trading onchain from the same app as the research
Due diligence on wallets and counterparties for crypto funds

fit: trade or invest in crypto and want onchain data on who holds what
run research at a crypto fund or trading desk
want wallet labels rather than raw blockchain explorers
not_fit: want a regulated, low-risk investment product

pricing.intro: Nansen's plans are shown inside the app after sign-in; its public plans link redirects to an account page. We do not quote prices we could not check on an official public page.

plans.name: Nansen plans
plans.detail: Subscription access to analytics and trading tools

pros: Very large set of labelled wallet addresses
Research and trading in one app
cons: Plan prices not shown on a public page

alternatives.intro: Other onchain analytics tools. We have not compared them hands-on.

items.name: Arkham
items.what: Onchain intelligence platform with entity labels
items.difference: Closest rival in wallet and entity labelling.

items.name: Dune
items.what: SQL queries and dashboards on blockchain data
items.difference: Community-built dashboards; you write queries yourself.

items.name: Glassnode
items.what: Onchain market metrics for Bitcoin and Ethereum
items.difference: Focus on market-wide metrics rather than wallet tracking.

faq.a: An onchain analytics platform that labels crypto wallet addresses so investors can track smart money and analyse tokens; it now also supports trading.
a16z led its $12 million Series A in 2021, and The Block reported a later round led by Accel at a $750 million valuation.
Plans are shown inside the app; we could not check them on a public page.
